text.p: German car components supplier Kolbenschmidt AG said on Thursday pre-tax profit in the five months to the end of February rose 3.5 million marks to 25.3 million marks.
Chairman Heinrich Binder, speaking to shareholders, predicted that sales and earnings would rise in the business year that ends on September 30 and said the company would resume dividend payments.
Kolbenschmidt has not paid a dividend for the past five years.
Sales in the first five months rose 3.9 percent to 561 million marks.
Binder said in a speech prepared for delivery at the annual general meeting that turnover would rise moderately in the full year and would "grow strongly" next year.
Profit growth would come particularly from improved cost structures.
